display.title: Tanya Shiur 43: Joy in True Faith, Tanya Chapter 33 (Lag BaOmer)
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 33: faith that nothing exists apart from Hashem, the double joy of making Him a home in this world, and a Lag BaOmer talk.
display.summary_long: Shiur 43 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series holds two sessions on chapter 33. The first, joined partway through, explains the true unity of Hashem: the world is nothing apart from Him, a faith inherited from Avraham Avinu. The prophet Chavakuk built all the mitzvos on faith, and joy is the sign that a person truly believes. The second session goes on: 'the tzaddik lives by his faith' makes every mitzvah alive. The Arizal prayed to do mitzvos as simply as a plain Jew, and the luz bone, fed by the Melave Malka meal, shows how faith revives like the resurrection of the dead. The joy is double: we rejoice that the King lives with us, and Hashem rejoices in His home below; the Tzemach Tzedek would give his whole Olam Haba for one pair of tzitzis. He explains the difference between restraining the yetzer hara and transforming it, with a memory of the Rebbe Rashab's talks being brought to the Frierdiker Rebbe; nature as hidden miracles; and the Frierdiker Rebbe's call to make America a place of Torah. He closes with 'Yismach Yisroel b'osav', one of the Rebbe's Twelve Pesukim, and the joy of Lag BaOmer that week.
display.lesson: Living with the faith that Hashem is everywhere makes every mitzvah alive and fills a Jew with joy, and his mitzvos in turn give joy to Hashem.

study_text.note: Two sessions: the end of one on the opening of ch. 33, then a session from 'b'emunaso yichyeh' to the end of the chapter; the next is announced as ch. 34.

date.note: Second session: 'this week is Lag BaOmer, on Thursday'. Lag BaOmer fell on Thursday in 5738 (also 5745, 5748); 5738 best fits the series after shiur 29 in Elul 5736.

segments.title: Tanya 33: the true unity and faith
segments.summary: First session (joined partway): nothing exists apart from Hashem, all mitzvos rest on faith, and joy is its proof.

segments.title: Shema written on parchment
segments.summary: The highest words are written on the lowliest material, a mitzvah done purely because Hashem commanded it.

segments.title: Tanya 33: the tzaddik lives by his faith
segments.summary: Second session: faith gives life to every mitzvah and brings a double joy, ours and Hashem's.

segments.title: The Arizal's prayer
segments.summary: Though he knew every secret of the mitzvos, the Arizal prayed to do them simply because Hashem commanded.

segments.title: The luz bone and Melave Malka
segments.summary: One bone, nourished only by the Melave Malka meal, survives for the resurrection, a picture of faith reviving a person.

segments.title: A double joy
segments.summary: We rejoice that the King lives with us, and Hashem rejoices in His home in this lowest world.

segments.title: The Tzemach Tzedek and the tzitzis
segments.summary: He would give his whole Olam Haba for one pair of tzitzis.

segments.title: Restraining and transforming the yetzer hara
segments.summary: Turning darkness into light; restraining the yetzer hara every day versus transforming it.

segments.title: The Rebbe Rashab's talks and the Frierdiker Rebbe
segments.summary: A memory of the first printing being brought to the Frierdiker Rebbe, who said one could live seventy years on that book; not doing is certain, not wanting may be self-deception.

segments.title: Kelipos, nature and hidden miracles
segments.summary: The kelipos hide G-dliness until the end of galus; nature is only miracles we have grown used to, which is why we thank Hashem every morning.

segments.title: Eretz Yisroel, the Diaspora and America
segments.summary: Light drawn from the darkest places gives Hashem the greatest joy, as the Frierdiker Rebbe said America too must become a place of Torah.

segments.title: Yismach Yisroel b'osav: one of the Twelve Pesukim
segments.summary: The passage the Rebbe chose for the Twelve Pesukim, and how mitzvos turn this divided world into a dwelling for His unity.

segments.title: Lag BaOmer, Rashbi's day of joy
segments.summary: Why the day a tzaddik passed away is a day of joy and light.

relations.note: Shiur 42 finishes chapter 32; this file opens partway into chapter 33, so a session may be missing between them.
